title: Buyer simulator setup card: Anu Hämäläinen, EVP & CFO, Kesko Oyj

blocks.text: Anu Hämäläinen, Executive Vice President, CFO (Kesko Oyj)

items.text: Net sales €12,474.1m in 2025 (estimate: company-reported figure from the 2025 Annual Report, not an estimate)
Comparable operating profit €654.9m in 2025, with full-year 2026 guidance narrowed to €670-730m
Approximately 18,991 employees at 2025 year-end, across grocery, building and technical, and car trade in the Nordics and Baltics
Dahl technical trade acquisition (Sweden, Norway, Denmark): debt-free price €1.2bn, completion targeted by end-2026, EU Commission unconditional approval received
Proposed €500-700m rights issue to refinance part of the bridge financing; EGM on 2026-10-30 (terms not yet set)
Stated ambition: Group net sales of some €20bn and division net sales of some €10bn in the early 2030s
Why are we adding a new vendor during an acquisition integration and a rights issue? Show me that this does not add integration risk or distract the Dahl team before close.
The €1.2bn price and the €500-700m raise are on the table. What is the payback on this spend, and how would you measure it in a way I can defend to the board and investors?
We already have Manhattan Associates for warehouse tooling and our own ERP and data programmes. What exactly do you do that they and our internal teams do not, and where does your work stop?

Dahl keeps separate brands and units. Any automation you propose must reconcile orders and financials across units without creating a new manual process. How do you handle that without a long data project?
Our 2026 guidance is €670-730m and we are watching margins closely. I will not approve a pilot that could move that range, and I will not accept vague productivity claims without a baseline.

blocks.text: Coaching: open with the Dahl integration and the margin guidance together. Lead with a single number: the estimated hours or cost per month that cross-unit reconciliation takes after close (estimate, to be validated with her team, not asserted as fact). Frame it as a question about where that effort sits, then offer a bounded first step that does not touch the Dahl close timeline. Avoid claims about Kesko's internal processes; present them as things you noticed publicly and want to test.
